question: May the studio run this component in the llc lane, judged by the terms of every input its shipped model was trained on?
rule: Pass only when every training input is identified and its terms, found in a primary source, permit commercial use. An input whose terms cannot be found fails the review as unverifiable.
component: SwiftF0 0.3.0 (lars76/swift-f0, tag v0.3.0, commit d1ba77f), MIT label on code and model
model: swift_f0/model.onnx, 135,090 bytes, git blob 3619f9ab7ad7c852b995550c74d971be236225d7. It is the same git blob as runs/seed1/model.onnx in lars76/swift-f0-training at a3095d2 ("Release 0.3.0"), whose README calls runs/seed1 the shipped model. The 0.3.0 changelog says the weights are unchanged from 0.2.0; only the exported graph changed (the 0.2.0 file is git blob 0b0411b1).
reasoning: The shipped run trained on the train split (train.tar) of the lars1234/pitch-benchmark dataset. Its compiler releases that compilation for research use under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and says it grants no rights beyond those of its sources.

Four of the nine third-party sources inside the split bar commercial use on their own terms: MDB-stem-synth (CC BY-NC 4.0), MOCHA-TIMIT (research, educational and individual use only), MUSDB18 (educational use only) and TAU Urban Acoustic Scenes 2019 (experimental and non-commercial use only; its licence counts distributing results achieved by use of the work as commercial use). NSynth, PTDB-TUG, CMU ARCTIC, LibriSpeech and RIRS_NOISES permit commercial use, and the coloured noise is generated by the training code.

Whether a trained model is adapted material of its training data, or a result achieved by using it, is legally unsettled. ADR-0011 (rules 5 to 7) resolves that doubt toward the narrower lanes: a permissive model label over non-commercial training data is not eligible for llc.

The row stays in individual and research with its permissive_label_nc_data release blocker. Every input was identified, so no unverified_training_data class applies. Only a written commercial permission from every blocking rights holder, or a model retrained on inputs that all permit commercial use, followed by a new review, could widen it.

training_inputs.name: pitch-benchmark train split (the compilation)
training_inputs.use: train.tar, SHA-256 974e33530a5d7cc37f3684be91783aed4b2cc235f6e5b5a6b3f68c73e52af206 in SHA256SUMS at dataset revision e98642f; the training README downloads it and passes it to train.py

terms.reading: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, for research use; grants no rights beyond those of its sources
CC BY-NC 4.0 (the record's Conditions of Use)

training_inputs.name: NSynth (train split)
training_inputs.use: corpus weight 0.15; acoustic instrument sources between 1046.5 and 2093.75 Hz only

training_inputs.name: PTDB-TUG
training_inputs.use: corpus weight 0.1667; labels are a consensus of classical trackers on the laryngograph channel

terms.reading: Open Database License 1.0; contents under the Database Contents License 1.0

training_inputs.note: ODbL permits commercial use; it asks for a notice on produced works and share-alike on derived databases

training_inputs.name: MOCHA-TIMIT
training_inputs.use: corpus weight 0.1667; speakers fsew0, msak0 and maps0 plus faet0, falh0, ffes0, fjmw0 and mjjn0 from unchecked/

terms.reading: research, educational and individual use only; not for commercial purposes without the authors' written permission

training_inputs.note: one LICENCE.txt sits at the top of the distribution; unchecked/ carries no other licence

training_inputs.name: CMU ARCTIC (bdl, jmk, slt)

terms.reading: free for use for any purpose, commercial or otherwise, keeping the copyright notice

training_inputs.note: festvox.org serves no HTTPS; the jmk and slt voices carry the same COPYING bytes

training_inputs.name: MUSDB18
training_inputs.use: music pool from stems 1 to 3 of 104 tracks; the 46 tracks shared with MedleyDB are excluded

terms.reading: educational purposes only; no commercial use without the express permission of the copyright holders

training_inputs.name: TAU Urban Acoustic Scenes 2019, development dataset
training_inputs.use: scene pool, taken from the hzhongresearch/tau2019 copy, which defers to the original licence

terms.reading: experimental and non-commercial purposes only; any commercial use is prohibited, including distributing results achieved by use of the work

training_inputs.name: coloured noise
training_inputs.use: shaped from white noise by augment.py during training

terms.reading: generated by the MIT-licensed training code; no third-party data

not_training_inputs.name: the eval.tar corpora (KEELE, FDA, APLAWD, AVID, OSF Glottis, Saarbruecken Voice Database, SpeechSynth, Vocadito, URMP, Bach10-mf0-synth) and their scene and room sources (DEMAND, AISHELL-3, MIR-1K accompaniment, RIRS_NOISES real impulse responses, OpenAIR)
not_training_inputs.why: the evaluation split only: build_eval renders them, build_train never reads them

not_training_inputs.name: the 0.1.x training mix (NSynth, PTDB-TUG, MIR-1K, MDB-stem-synth, SpeechSynth, CHiME-Home noise)
not_training_inputs.why: the paper describes SwiftF0 0.1.x; 0.2.0 replaced the network, and the 0.3.0 model comes from the swift-f0-training run

limits: No dataset, archive or weight file was downloaded. The contents of train.tar are read from config.py, the dataset card at e98642f and the preparation code at 6f21369 (unchanged since release 2.0.0, which introduced the prepared dataset). The training log records no archive hash.
The CMU ARCTIC licence was read in the unpacked voice directories, not inside the -WAVEGG archives the preparation code downloads.
Dynamic pages (Zenodo, Hugging Face API, Magenta, OpenSLR, TU Graz, GitHub API) are hashed as fetched; their bytes can change while their terms stay the same.
This review covers training data only. The MIT code and model label are T03's verified row.
